channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: ‘Sou um cara de jogo de cintura, mas não chego ao teatro rebolado’, diz Wagner sobre críticas ao STF
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), government leader in the Senate, says he will not collaborate in attacks on the Supreme Federal Court (STF), even when they come from his own party, stating he’d rather not return to office if he has to 'come back disguised'. Although he supported a 2023 PEC to limit individual STF rulings, he criticizes the 'frenzy' of attacking the Court and notes that political timing differs from the justices’ sphere, which he describes as 'another bubble'. Wagner, running for re-election in 2026, spoke during the PT’s 8th Congress, where a code of ethics for the STF is being debated, following the Banco Master scandal that strained Lula’s relationship with the Court.

item.title: A criminalização do dissenso vai se tornando regra e não é um bom prenúncio para o ano eleitoral
item.description: Fernando Schüler criticizes the criminalization of dissent in Brazil, noting that the inclusion of former governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry over a political satire sets a dangerous precedent for freedom of expression. He contrasts current repression with historical tolerance by figures like Emperor Pedro II, José Sarney, and Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who accepted criticism and satire as democratic norms. Schüler argues that this pattern, beginning in 2019 with the fake news investigation, now threatens opposition candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro with potential ineligibility and signals a troubling outlook for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula defende acordo UE-Mercosul e propõe Portugal como porta de entrada para empresas brasileiras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended the Mercosul-European Union agreement during a visit to Lisbon and proposed Portugal as a gateway for Brazilian companies into the European market. He praised globalization and emphasized the importance of international cooperation for Brazil's economic development.

item.title: Nikolas posta meme após nova cobrança de apoio a Flávio
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) posted a meme on X after being criticized by Bolsonarists for allegedly lacking support for Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) presidential bid. According to Folha de S.Paulo, he mentioned Flávio in only 10 of his 544 posts on the platform. The meme served as an indirect response to loyalty pressures within the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Tarcísio: “Talvez gastemos muita energia com polarização que não nos leva a nada”
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized Brazil's political polarization during a speech in Ouro Preto (MG) while receiving the Great Collar of the Inconfidência Mineira. Without directly naming President Lula, he suggested the country may be wasting excessive energy on conflicts that lead to no productive outcomes.

item.title: Lula sopesa aplicar “la reciprocidad” a Estados Unidos tras la expulsión de un enlace policial brasileño en Florida
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva condemned the expulsion of a Brazilian police liaison by U.S. authorities, stating Brazil will respond in kind under the principle of reciprocity. He accused the U.S. government of abusing its power and renewed his criticism of former President Donald Trump, citing growing tensions in bilateral relations amid delays in a planned meeting and the proximity of a closely contested U.S. election.

item.title: Tarcísio recebe medalha em MG e critica polarização no país
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas received the Great Collar of the Inconfidência in Ouro Preto (MG) and criticized political polarization in Brazil, questioning whether the heroes of the Inconfidência Mineira would be satisfied with the country's current state. He also praised former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema for his fiscally responsible administration.

item.title: Lula ironiza Trump: ‘É importante que a gente dê logo o Prêmio Nobel da Paz’
item.description: President Lula ironically suggested that Donald Trump should immediately receive the Nobel Peace Prize after Trump claimed to have ended eight wars without being awarded it. The remark was made in Lisbon during Lula’s European tour, where he lamented the lack of any institution capable of fostering global peace.

item.title: Oposição articula novo pedido de impeachment de Gilmar Mendes após pedido para incluir Zema no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Opposition lawmakers announced a new impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes after he sought to include former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry over a satirical video. The opposition argues the move criminalizes institutional criticism and threatens free speech, calling it a dangerous precedent for democracy.

item.title: Zema compara ministros do STF a coroa portuguesa em vídeo sobre inconfidência mineira
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), a pre-candidate for president, compared STF ministers to the Portuguese crown in a social media video, stating that 'in place of the Portuguese crown sit the untouchables of Brasília'. The remark was made in reference to the Inconfidência Mineira, a historical movement resisting central authority.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro anuncia 'levantamento' de prefeitos e vereadores do PL que 'não divulgam' a candidatura de Flávio
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro announced he will conduct a survey of PL mayors and council members who are not publicizing his brother Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, aiming to correct their stance through party leadership. He criticized the lack of political expression and urged supporters to respectfully expose omissions by fellow party members. The move reflects growing internal divisions within the Brazilian right, including recent clashes with Eduardo and Nikolas Bolsonaro.

item.title: Líder evangélico sinaliza apoio à pré-candidatura de Caiado, mas cita que 'temos dois candidatos maravilhosos de direita'
item.description: Evangelical leader Apostle César Augusto praised Ronaldo Caiado as a longtime friend and conservative values defender but avoided explicit endorsement, stating 'we have two wonderful right-wing candidates,' also referencing Flávio Bolsonaro. Caiado highlighted his record in Goiás and thanked the apostle’s blessings, while the event featured PSD president Gilberto Kassab and São Paulo mayor Ricardo Nunes.

item.title: Dino e Cármen seguem Moraes e condenam Eduardo Bolsonaro por crime contra Tabata Amaral
item.description: The STF virtual plenary has recorded three votes for the conviction of Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against federal deputy Tabata Amaral, with justices Alexandre de Moraes (relator), Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino supporting the guilty verdict. The proposed sentence is one year of detention in an open regime, with aggravating factors due to the victim being a public servant and the crime being committed via the internet. The case remains open for judgment until October 28, allowing other justices to vote or express dissenting opinions.

item.title: Lula promete reciprocidade após governo Trump determinar saída de delegado da PF que atuou na prisão de Ramagem
item.description: President Lula promised reciprocity after the U.S. government formally requested the departure of Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo, who had been involved in the arrest of former bolsonarist deputy Alexandre Ramagem. Lula stated he would not accept U.S. interference and would respond in kind against U.S. officials in Brazil. The case centers on international police cooperation and allegations of U.S. authority abuse.

item.title: Alckmin nomeia novo ministro do Empreendedorismo
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin appointed Paulo Henrique Rodrigues Pereira as Minister of Entrepreneurship, Microenterprise and Small Business while President Lula is in Europe. Pereira, a USP law professor and former national justice secretary under Ricardo Lewandowski, replaces Tadeu Alencar, who moves to a special advisory role in the vice-presidency before returning to Congress. The appointment reflects PSB party influence, backed by João Campos and Márcio França.

item.title: Chega protesta contra presença de Lula em Lisboa
item.description: The Chega party held a protest against the presence of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Lisbon, in front of Belém Palace, during his official visit for meetings with Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro and President António José Seguro. The demonstration was led by Chega president André Ventura, who criticized Brazil's foreign policy. The protest took place on Tuesday afternoon, the 21st.

item.title: Lula avalia responder com 'reciprocidade' à expulsão pelos EUA de delegado da PF
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that he is considering responding with 'reciprocity' to the expulsion by the United States of a Federal Police delegate linked to the case of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL/RJ). The comment was made on Tuesday (21), amid renewed diplomatic tensions between Brazil and the U.S.

item.title: Imprensa francesa analisa ofensiva bolsonarista contra o STF e recuo da esquerda entre jovens
item.description: French press highlights that Brazil's political landscape is entering the pre-electoral period with intensified attacks by allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro against the Supreme Federal Court (STF), while the left is losing ground among young voters. This dynamic reflects growing polarization, with Bolsonarism betting on institutional confrontation and the left losing space in a key electoral segment.

item.title: Lula e PT divulgam nota de pesar pela morte de Valmir Chaves, um dos fundadores do MST
item.description: President Lula issued a statement of condolence for the death of Valmir Rodrigues Chaves, known as Bill, one of the founders of the MST, during his European visit. In the message, Lula highlighted Chaves' 40 years of dedication to the struggle for land rights and agrarian reform.

item.title: “Se Tiradentes vivesse hoje, já teria se revoltado contra Lula”, diz Moro
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) criticized Lula's fiscal policy on Tiradentes Day, claiming the historical revolutionary figure would revolt today against the government's taxes. The statement was posted on X (formerly Twitter) and reinforces Moro's role as a federal government opponent.

item.title: Valdemar vai até Eduardo nos EUA para destravar chapa ao Senado por SP
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto and André do Prado met with Eduardo Bolsonaro in the U.S. to decide the PL's Senate candidate for São Paulo, as Eduardo is considered the 'owner' of the seat. The goal is to nominate Prado, an ally of Governor Tarcísio, to kickstart the pre-campaign for the state ticket.

item.title: Governador de MG diz ter 'inveja branca' de Tarcísio por nomear 1ª mulher chefe da PM; veja vídeo
item.description: The governor of Minas Gerais, Mateus Simões (PSD), said he felt 'white envy' toward his São Paulo counterpart, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), for appointing the first woman as commander-general of the São Paulo Military Police. Simões made the remark during a press conference, praising the initiative for advancing gender representation in security forces. A video of his comments was released by local media.

item.title: Entenda as diferenças dos projetos de redução da jornada e fim da 6 X 1
item.description: President Lula's government proposes reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours via ordinary law, mandating two consecutive paid rest days (5×2 model) with no salary reduction, effective immediately upon sanction. Meanwhile, Congress is advancing three constitutional amendments (PECs) to reduce the workweek to 36 hours, with a transition period of up to 10 years: PEC 221/2019 (Reginaldo Lopes) lacks detail on rest distribution, while PEC 8/2025 (Erika Hilton) proposes a 4×3 model (4 work days, 3 rest days); both remain subject to change in the special committee.

item.title: PL do fim da 6 X 1 fixa duas folgas consecutivas por semana
item.description: President Lula's bill sent to Congress proposes reducing the weekly workday from 44 to 40 hours, granting two consecutive 48-hour days off per week, preferably on weekends, without salary reduction. The text preserves the 11-hour inter-shift rest and allows flexibility in the 12X36 regime via collective agreement, as long as the 40-hour weekly limit is respected.

item.title: 'Portugal pode ser a grande porta da entrada dos interesses empresariais brasileiros', diz Lula em Lisboa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva emphasized during a visit to Lisbon that Portugal could serve as a gateway for Brazilian business interests in Europe, underscoring the importance of economic cooperation between the two nations. He praised the historical and cultural ties between Brazil and Portugal and highlighted the potential to expand Brazilian investments in sectors such as energy, technology, and infrastructure in Portuguese territory. The statement was made after fulfilling commitments in Germany, as part of a European tour aimed at strengthening trade and strategic partnerships.

item.title: Lula se despede da Europa em Portugal e diz que viagem foi ʽmaravilhosaʼ
item.description: Lula concluded his European trip in Portugal, where he had lunch with President António José Seguro at the Belém Palace. He described the journey as 'wonderful' in a brief statement before departing. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Após ação de Gilmar, Zema divulga novo vídeo para criticar 'intocáveis' e compara ministros com Coroa Portuguesa
item.description: Romeu Zema, a pre-candidate for the Presidency, intensified his criticism of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) during Tiradentes’ Day, comparing the justices to the Portuguese Crown and labeling them 'untouchables'. He denounced a supposed moment of 'moral shame' in Brazil, accusing the Court of privileges and abuses, after Minister Gilmar Mendes filed a criminal complaint against him over a satirical video mocking STF rulings. Zema claimed the fight for freedom remains alive and that the 2026 elections will decide whether the 'untouchables' or 'decent Brazilians' will govern the country.

item.title: Ramagem e esposa reagem à expulsão de delegado da PF dos EUA
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem and his wife Rebeca reacted to the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho from the United States following his involvement in Ramagem’s arrest. The U.S. Embassy in Brazil stated that no foreigner can manipulate its immigration system to circumvent formal extradition requests or extend political persecution. Rebeca called the move 'the cowardice of the weak,' while Ramagem reposted the embassy’s statement and shared his wife’s Instagram post.

item.title: Portugueses e brasileiros protestam contra Lula em Lisboa
item.description: Portuguese and Brazilian protesters gathered in Lisbon to demonstrate against President Lula's visit, organized by the Chega party on anti-corruption grounds. Simultaneously, PT supporters in Lisbon held a pro-Lula rally near the same location. Both events took place near Belém Palace and drew approximately 300 participants each.

item.title: Lula exalta luta e lamenta morte de Bill, um dos fundadores do MST
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva mourned the death of Valmir Rodrigues Chaves, known as Bill, one of the founders of the Landless Workers' Movement (MST). Bill passed away on April 20 after 60 days in intensive care in São Paulo, and Lula praised his over four-decade-long struggle for land rights, better living conditions for small farmers, and food sovereignty.

item.title: Alckmin fala em aguardar antes de revidar os EUA
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) said Brazil should wait for developments in the case involving a Federal Police delegate in the U.S. before taking retaliatory measures, despite Lula’s promise of reciprocity. He also stressed that BRB investigations must proceed swiftly but without premature conclusions, and reiterated that the federal government will not bail out the bank, which may have suffered losses exceeding R$ 50 billion.

item.title: Com IA, Tarcísio promove versão turbinada da "Times Square Paulistana"
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas shared an AI-generated video on social media showcasing an enhanced version of the 'Boulervad São João' project, nicknamed 'Times Square Paulistana'. The initiative proposes installing luminous panels along São João Avenue, totaling 2.100m² of LED screens and a projection on the blind façade of the Edifício Independência, aiming to modernize the city center with cultural, informational, and service content, despite criticism for relaxing the Clean City Law.

item.title: Crusoé: Carlos Bolsonaro anuncia fiscalização de apoio a Flávio
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro announced he is conducting a survey of mayors, councilors, party leaders, local branches, and Liberal Party members to determine who supports or does not support the presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. He said it is 'staggering' to see that the overwhelming majority of these political figures are not publicly endorsing the pre-candidate. The effort aims to map internal party support for Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential bid within the PL.

item.title: “É importante dar logo Nobel da Paz para Trump”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula (PT) said, in a provocative tone, that it is important to 'give right away' the Nobel Peace Prize to Donald Trump to end wars worldwide. The comment was made during a joint press conference with Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro in the Jardim...

item.title: Lula: OMC “nunca mais funcionou” depois da eleição de Obama
item.description: Lula criticized the WTO for ceasing to function after Barack Obama’s 2008 election, accusing wealthy nations of hypocrisy for promoting free trade in the 1980s and then adopting protectionism as developing countries became competitive. He defended multilateralism, praised the Mercosul-EU agreement as provisionally valid from May 1, and stressed Brazil’s neutrality in seeking balanced relations with China, the U.S., Russia, and all other partners.

item.title: Bolsonaro, Caiado e Tarcísio são “traidores da pátria”, diz Gleisi
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) labeled members of the Bolsonaro family, former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado, and São Paulo governor Tarcísio de Freitas as 'traitors of the homeland' in reference to the Tiradentes holiday. The statement was made on March 21 during a political demonstration, linking the figures to actions against national interests. The remark reflects growing political polarization in Brazil, with the PT accusing opposition figures of undermining national sovereignty and democratic values.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Projeções eleitorais para Lula e Flávio
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program highlighted a Quaest poll indicating an unfavorable scenario for President Lula ahead of the 2026 election campaign. It also noted that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, is successfully strengthening his political image in the current context.

item.title: “A luta dos inconfidentes ainda não acabou”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president from the Novo party, reiterated his criticisms of Supreme Court ministers, stating that 'the fight of the inconfidentes is not over'. He did not retreat despite an investigation request by Gilmar Mendes, who sought to include him in the fake news inquiry, and released a video on a holiday maintaining his confrontational stance toward the Court.

item.title: Lula diz que Parlamento Europeu errou ao contestar o Mercosul-UE
item.description: Lula criticized the European Parliament for attempting to judicially suspend the Mercosul-EU trade agreement, calling it a 'very big mistake' and arguing that international trade only works when neither side seeks to harm the other. He emphasized the complementarity between the blocs and positioned Portugal as a gateway for Brazilian business interests in Europe. The agreement is set to take provisional effect on May 1, 2026.

item.title: Lula ironiza e sugere dar Nobel da Paz a Trump para ‘não ter mais guerra’
item.description: Lula ironically suggested awarding the Nobel Peace Prize to Donald Trump to 'end all wars', noting that Trump frequently claims to have resolved global conflicts without receiving the prize. The remark was made during a joint statement with Portugal's Prime Minister in Lisbon, where Lula also warned that the world now faces more conflicts than since World War II. He further criticized Trump's stance on the Middle East, the Pope, and Cuba.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: cientista político alerta para um ponto ‘enganoso’ nas pesquisas de 2º turno
item.description: Political scientist Antonio Lavareda warns that current polls showing a polarized race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro reflect more the candidates' visibility than a consolidated voter choice, due to high electorate volatility and low recall of other candidates. He notes that 43% of voters say they could still change their vote, and even those who claim to have decided are not immune to shifts from new information, debates, or unexpected events. Lavareda emphasizes that second-round simulations at this stage have low predictive power, citing historical failures in 2022 and 1998 when polls significantly mispredicted the actual outcomes.

item.title: Diante de Lula, Portugal minimiza xenofobia e realça regularizações de brasileiros
item.description: Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro downplayed allegations of xenophobia against Brazilians during a meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, describing the incidents as isolated despite rising complaints. Montenegro highlighted the regularization of 235,000 Brazilian immigration cases over the past two years and noted that 5,000 applications were rejected for failing to meet requirements, while omitting reference to a recently passed anti-immigration law supported by the far-right Chega party. Lula avoided delving into the issue, instead praising the contributions of Brazilians in Portugal and referencing Tiradentes’ Day as a symbol of Brazil’s independence struggle.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil e Portugal vivem “melhor momento”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil and Portugal are experiencing the best moment in their historical relationship during a visit to Lisbon, emphasizing the goal of using Portugal as a base for Brazilian business expansion in Europe and citing Embraer as a successful model. He also discussed immigration, criticizing Portugal’s new nationality law that tightens citizenship rules for foreigners, affecting thousands of Brazilians living in the country, and noted both opposing and supportive protests during his stay in Lisbon.

item.title: Lula: comércio em outras moedas é desejo, mas a discussão é do Banco Central
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that reducing the use of the dollar in commercial transactions is a government desire, but the decision lies with the Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance, not the presidency. He reiterated his support for using local currencies in international trade, particularly within BRICS, and criticized the war in Iran as unnecessary, claiming a 2010 agreement between Brazil, Turkey, and Iran had already resolved the uranium enrichment issue.

item.title: STF fragmentado leva ministros a proporem soluções próprias para a crise no Judiciário
item.description: In 2026, the STF is fragmented, with each justice proposing individual solutions to the judiciary crisis: Gilmar Mendes pursues direct confrontation with critics via criminal complaints and investigations, while Edson Fachin advocates for a Code of Conduct as an internal self-correction mechanism. Flávio Dino, meanwhile, supports a deeper structural reform of the judiciary from within, contrasting with the more incremental approaches of his peers.

item.title: Em Portugal, Lula lamenta caráter provisório do acordo UE-Mercosul: ‘Um erro’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the provisional nature of the EU-Mercosul agreement during a visit to Portugal, calling it a 'mistake' and a 'major error' by the European Parliament for filing a legal challenge. Lula argued the deal does not threaten European agriculture but offers complementary opportunities, dismissing European concerns as 'nonsense' and advocating for a more sophisticated, multilateral-based relationship with the EU.

item.title: Lula afirma que Brasil e Portugal vivem melhor momento da relação e exalta brasileiros no país: 'Povo trabalhador'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated during a visit to Portugal that Brazil and the country are experiencing their best bilateral relations ever, praising Brazilians as hardworking, skilled professionals contributing to Portugal’s middle class through home purchases and labor integration. He also criticized global unilateralism and the weakening of the UN, thanked Portugal for supporting the Mercosul-EU agreement, and jokingly said Donald Trump should 'win' the Nobel Peace Prize soon to end world wars.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil adotará reciprocidade contra EUA se for constatado abuso na remoção de agente da PF que atuou na prisão de Ramagem
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil will adopt reciprocity measures against the United States if it is proven that the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho — who participated in the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem on U.S. soil — was an abuse. Lula condemned the action as interference and an abuse of authority by figures tied to the Trump government, emphasizing Brazil will not accept such interventions. The case relates to Ramagem’s conviction for attempted coup and his fugitive status after fleeing to the U.S.

item.title: Polícia Federal nomeia delegada para posto de servidor expulso dos EUA
item.description: The Federal Police appointed delegate Tatiana Alves Torres to replace Marcelo Ivo as liaison officer at ICE following his expulsion by the U.S., which accused him of attempting to manipulate the immigration system and extending political persecution. President Lula denounced the expulsion as an 'abuse' and stated Brazil may respond with reciprocity against U.S. officials in Brazil. The change was formalized by a portaria signed by Federal Police General Director Andrei Rodrigues and published in the Official Gazette.

item.title: Lula põe Trump no colo de Flávio
item.description: Lula stated that a potential interference by Trump in Brazil’s succession would greatly help him, suggesting the former U.S. president could influence the political landscape in his favor. The remark was made shortly before departing for Europe, sparking speculation about external alliances in the 2026 election race.
